one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban announces that on August 29, 2025 at the Manila Polo Club in Makati -- with First Lady Louise Araneta-Marcos as special guest and Fernando Zobel de Ayala as guest speaker -- the Foundation for Liberty and Prosperity will award 20 law scholarships at P250,000 each (P5M, via Tan Yan Kee Foundation), 5 ESMEL MBA fellowships at P500,000 each (P2.5M, via Metro Pacific Investments Foundation, covering entrepreneurship, sustainability, management, economics, or business law), and roughly P1M in dissertation prizes (via Ayala Corp.). He names the full rosters: ten third-year law scholars (Acidre, Caliosan, Humarang, Mabelin, Manalo, Poquiz, Reambonanza, Tumolva, Unabia, Vergara), ten fourth-year scholars (Bellen, Despi, Mirasol, Mutuc, Orajay, Paguia, Sobreviñas, Te, Viernes, Villareal), the five ESMEL fellows (Balagtas, Domingo, Geronimo, Santos, So -- all three AIM fellows enrolling in AIM's new eight-month-built Master's in International Business Law program led by Dr. Jikeong Kang with Profs. Olivier Roche and Felipe Calderon), and the dissertation winners headed by Isabelle Ginez (1st, P320k) and Laurice Sy (2nd, P220k) with three P120k third-placers and four P20k finalists. He details the three Boards of Judges -- for law scholarships (chaired by CJ Gesmundo), for ESMEL (chaired by ret. BSP Gov. Tetangco), and for dissertations (chaired by SC Justice Jhosep Y. Lopez) -- and lays out the FLP board of trustees and officers. Threaded through the announcement is his philosophical refrain that 'knowledge of the law rounds out business thinking' -- telling entrepreneurs not only what they cannot do but how far they can go -- and his belief that the best way to nurture prosperity is to help Filipinos help themselves through private entrepreneurship under the rule of law, the founding philosophy FLP has carried since 2011.
